validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated pipeline. Docket CP17-66-000: Venture Global Plaquemines LNG, LLC and Venture Global Gator Express, LLC filed an NGA application on Feb 28, 2017 (Federal Register notice of application, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2017/03/22/2017-05671/venture-global-plaquemines-lng-llc-and-venture-global-gator-express-llc-notice-of-application, published 2017-03-22 restating the Feb 28, 2017 filing date). FERC's certificate order (issued 2019, PDF at https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-06/20190930152330-CP17-66-000.pdf) authorizes construction of 'Gator Express' -- 15 miles of 42-inch pipeline, 1,970,000 Dth/day capacity, interconnecting with Tennessee Gas Pipeline and Texas Eastern Transmission in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana. A 2023 Federal Register notice (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/01/13/2023-00548/venture-global-plaquemines-lng-llc-gator-express-pipeline-llc-notice-of-amendment-of-authorization) confirms an amendment of authorization for 'Gator Express Pipeline LLC' tied to the same Plaquemines LNG project. Independent confirmation the pipe was actually built and is flowing gas: Natural Gas Intel (2024, https://naturalgasintel.com/news/portion-of-plaquemines-lngs-2-bcfd-pipeline-project-ready-for-service-venture-global-says/), East Daley Analytics (2025-01, https://www.eastdaley.com/media-and-news/plaquemines-lng-takes-first-gas-in-project-milestone and https://eastdaley.com/media-and-news/plaquemines-lng-start-lifts-kmi-enbridge-pipes), and Venture Global's own project page (https://ventureglobal.com/venture-global-plaquemines/plaquemines-pipeline/, describing a 15-mile, 42-inch pipeline built in two segments). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- an interstate NGA-certificated transmission lateral feeding an LNG terminal, not a gathering/production line; EIA's dated Aug2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release (Historical Projects (1996-2024) tab, row 1121) lists Pipeline Type=Interstate, Authority=FERC for this row, consistent with interstate FERC jurisdiction (cite corrected 2026-09-11 from the undated, quarterly-changing EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, banned by the batch rules). DUPLICATE: NOT the same pipe as P5519 (Texas Eastern Transmission / TETCO Venice Extension) -- different applicant/owner (Venture Global vs. Enbridge/TETCO), different FERC docket, different physical corridor (Gator Express interconnects TGP+Texas Eastern into Plaquemines LNG from the west/interior side; TETCO's Venice Extension is TETCO's own lateral looping/replacing an existing line). Both merely share the same downstream customer (Plaquemines LNG) -- an interconnection relationship, not identity. Also NOT the same PID as Gator Express Phase 2 (P3193), which is out of this batch's scope (batch A2) and covers a later, separate compression/expansion scope. ATTRIBUTION: see the separate caveat record on Owner1 naming (Venture Global Gator Express, LLC vs. Gator Express Pipeline LLC) -- a naming-history nuance, not a wrong owner. LOCATION: Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana confirmed by both the FERC order and EIA workbook; feeding the Plaquemines LNG terminal per Venture Global's own site.

However, the ORIGINAL 2017 NGA application and the FERC certificate order both identify the applicant/certificate holder as 'Venture Global Gator Express, LLC' (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2017/03/22/2017-05671/... and https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-06/20190930152330-CP17-66-000.pdf). Both name forms trace to FERC-filed documents (one origin, not independent of each other), so this is filed as a caveat rather than a correction: either the entity was renamed between 2017 and 2023, or the two names are used interchangeably by the sponsor/FERC across different years. Recommend verifying against a corporate registry before treating the sheet value as wrong -- it is currently the better-sourced (more recent) of the two names.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's own cited ref (East Daley 'takes first gas' article) is itself the newest, on-point evidence that this row is stale: the pipeline has been in service since November 2024, not under construction. Newest dated evidence: East Daley Analytics, 2025-01-29 ('PLNG start lifts KMI, Enbridge pipes' and 'Plaquemines LNG takes first gas in project milestone'), reporting active gas flows (approx. 1.2-1.3 Bcf/d) through the Gator Express meters as of January 2025, using past-tense/completed-construction language. Independently corroborated by (1) the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which lists 'Gator Express Pipeline (Phase 1)' as Status='Completed' with an in-service date of 2024-11-01, matching FERC's authorization to place the facilities into service (granted 2024-11-27 per the docket), and (2) Natural Gas Intel's 2024 report that a portion of the Plaquemines LNG feed-gas pipeline system was ready for service. Two independent origins (East Daley's trade analytics desk and EIA's independently-compiled dataset) agree the pipeline is operating, not under construction -- recommending Status='operating' with StartYear1=2024/StartMonth1=11 sourced to the EIA in-service date. This directly answers this batch's prompt for construction-status rows (P0193 named explicitly): NOW IN SERVICE. EIA follow-up (2026-09-10): cite corrected to the dated Aug2026 EIA release (was the undated, quarterly-changing EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, banned by the batch rules); per eia_projects_long.csv, Phase 1 first reads 'Complete' in the 2025-01 release and holds 'Complete'/'Completed' through 2026-08 with no reversal, and the fills-level Status [ref] unit (previously UNRESOLVED at that layer) is now closed as REFS_ADDED with this same EIA source.
